newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan proposes 4.1 pct rise in 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan proposes 4.1 pct rise in 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Taiwan's cabinet on Thursday proposed to parliament a budget of T$1.2435 trillion for fiscal year 1997/98, a 4.1 percent increase of the previous year's spending plan.

The proposed budget, which now goes to the Legislative Yuan for debate and approval, plans for a T$122.9 billion deficit, down an annual 20 percent, and allocates T$260.2 billion in defence spending, a year-on-year rise of 3.1 percent.

The defence portion of the budget, despite its rise in dollar terms, actually shrinks in terms of its percentage of overall spending at 20.9 percent -- down 0.2 percentage points from the previous budget.
The defence portion of the budget includes T$47.4 billion earmarked for purchase of advanced fighters from France and the United States, part of a nine-year T$300.7 billion fighter procurement fund.
Taiwan maintains that it needs the 60 French-made Mirage and 150 U.S.-made F16 fighters to counter a steady modernisation of arch rival communist China's the three-million strong military.

The budget proposes issuing T$100 billion in construction bonds to help ease the deficit, according to Wei Duan, head of the cabinet's Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics who publicly disclosed the spending plan.
